problem: Memory-based discrete VLN agents (e.g. GridMM) with frozen weights suffer from stale or redundant evidence at memory readout and from wasteful immediate backtracking/short loops at action selection, and fixing these usually needs retraining or heavier planners.
motivation: Improving a pretrained navigator at inference time without retraining or architecture changes is practical. Stale memory slots add noise to aggregation, and immediate reversals lengthen trajectories and runtime without necessarily causing failure.
key_idea: A training-free test-time layer that reweights memory slots at readout by age, visit count and novelty (Test-Time Memory Decay) and subtracts a next-hop penalty from candidate scores to discourage immediate reversals (Anti-Loop Regularization).
insight: Conservative read-side decay preserves or improves accuracy and cuts runtime, whereas write-side memory rewriting (update-only, full-mode) is less stable and often hurts (e.g. R2R test SR 72, SPL 59-60 vs 73/62 baseline), so a frozen policy is disturbed by altered stored representations. The behavior analysis shows decay alone does not reduce backtracking (R2R 2.30% to 3.51%), and anti-loop lowers it (to 2.01% on R2R, 8.45% to 5.99% on REVERIE) with shorter trajectories, so the two modules act at different stages.
method: Slot metadata: per memory slot keep age a_i, visit count c_i, and novelty n_i (EMA, rho=0.5, of 1-cos between old and new slot features).
Memory decay readout weight: w_i = clip(exp(-lambda a_i)(1-alpha c_i/(c_i+1))(0.5+0.5 n_i), 0.35, 1.0), applied only when aggregating memory; stored content is unchanged.
Anti-loop next-hop penalty: p_t(v)=beta_back*I[h(v)=v_{t-1}]+beta_rev*I[visit(h(v))>=k], where h(v) is the first hop toward candidate v; s'=s-p before argmax (beta_back=0.22, beta_rev=0.06, k=2).
Plug-in inference: no learnable parameters, the GridMM backbone, stop head and checkpoints stay unchanged; the penalty is finite and nothing is masked, so backtracking is still possible.
Write-side variants (stress tests): update-only uses a heuristic gate to refresh matched slots and append unmatched ones; full-mode combines it with decay.

setting.training_data: none (training-free; reuses the baseline GridMM checkpoints)
setting.observation: panoramic RGB views on discrete viewpoint graph with explicit grid memory
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (argmax over candidate nodes)

numbers.extra: training-free test-time control; runtime 666.37 s on RTX 5070 Ti
numbers.evidence: Table 1 Results on the R2R dataset, decay+anti-loop row, Val Unseen
Table 2 Results on the REVERIE val-unseen split, decay+anti-loop row

numbers_note: R2R SR/SPL are printed as integers in the paper. The GridMM baseline was re-run by the authors with runtime measured on an RTX 5070 Ti. REVERIE test is not reported because the server is unavailable.
results: On the GridMM baseline, decay+anti-loop improves R2R val-unseen SR/SPL from 74/64 to 76/66, cuts TL from 13.27 to 12.41 and runtime from 937.99 s to 666.37 s. On REVERIE val-unseen it raises SR/SPL/RGSPL from 51.37/36.47/24.56 to 52.34/37.53/25.44 and cuts runtime from 4329.67 s to 1497.98 s. R2R test NE is slightly worse (3.38 vs 3.35).
limitations: Validated only on a GridMM-based navigator, so transfer to other memory backbones is untested.
Gains are small (about 1-2 points), the hyperparameters are heuristic and hand-set, and the R2R test NE gets slightly worse; runtime is measured on one machine and is not comparable across papers.
Restricted to deterministic argmax decoding in discrete VLN; stochastic decoding and continuous navigation are not evaluated.
